The '''Women's FIH Hockey World Cup''' is the [[field hockey]] World Cup competition for women, whose format for qualification and the final tournament is similar to the men's. It has been held since 1974. The tournament has been organized by the [[International Hockey Federation]] (FIH) since they merged with the International Federation of Women's Hockey Associations (IFWHA) in 1982. Since [[1986 Women's World Hockey Cup|1986]], it has been held regularly once every four years, in the same year as the men's competition, which is mid-cycle between Summer Olympic games.

Of the sixteen tournaments held, only four teams have won the event. [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] is the most successful team, having won the title nine times. [[Argentina women's national field hockey team|Argentina]] has won three titles; [[Germany women's national field hockey team|Germany]] and [[Hockeyroos|Australia]] have won two titles each. The Netherlands, Australia and Germany are able to defend their titles. At the end of the 2026 World Cup, fifteen nations had reached the semifinal of the tournament.

The size of the tournament has changed over time. The 1974 and 1978 World Cups featured 10 nations (smallest); the 1976 World Cup featured 11 nations; the 2002 World Cup featured 16 nations (largest), and the remaining seven World Cups have featured 12 nations. The World Cup was again expanded to 16 teams in 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=World Cup field to expand to 16 teams in 2018|url=http://www.fih.ch/en/news-3991-world-cup-field-to-expand-to-16-teams-in|access-date=2012-11-03|newspaper=FIH|date=2012-11-01}}</ref>

The 2022 tournament was held in [[Amstelveen]] and [[Terrassa]] from 1–17 July, with [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] winning a third consecutive title and a record ninth title after beating [[Argentina women's national field hockey team|Argentina]] 3–1 in the final.
